text: Mara opens the rule's configured source: 198.51.0.0/16. The vendor's own onboarding paperwork documents their real range as 198.51.100.16/28. The two numbers don't match.
A /28 covers 16 addresses -- the vendor's whole real range. A /16 covers 65,536 addresses. The vendor's range sits entirely inside the configured one, which is exactly why nothing looked broken.
The rule's change history shows it was created the night of Lesson 4's deadline-pressured setup and never revisited since. No process existed to bring its scope back up for review.
This isn't a story about carelessness so much as a plausible typo under time pressure, with no trigger that would ever surface it again.
Any address inside that 65,536-address range could have reached the jump host's RDP port the whole time the rule existed. The 3 AM alert is the first time one actually got noticed.
